tasks.short: Read work orders and determine the painting requirements.

steps.what: Read the work orders for this painting job.
inputs: order card when the supervisor has written one
outputs: the rooms, colour, and who asked, as the work order states them

steps.what: Receive instructions from supervisors or homeowners.
inputs: the rooms, colour, and who asked, as the work order states them

steps.what: Determine the work requirements and record them.
inputs: the rooms, colour, and who asked, as the work order states them
outputs: the work requirements the painter recorded for this job

tasks.design: The supervisor keeps a paper order card: the job, the rooms, the colour, and who asked. The painter reads that card, or the paper work order when a row is missing, then receives instructions from the supervisor or the homeowner and determines the work requirements. Hearing the instructions and determining the requirements stay at full time.
tasks.previous_blocker: The written order sat in a pile, so each job started as a search. The homeowner's instructions exist only in the conversation.
tasks.enabler_now: The supervisor already knows the job, the rooms, the colour, and who asked. Writing those four fields on a card needs no new system and no model.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing the instructions, and deciding what the job actually requires, stay with the painter.
tasks.human_edge: Judging the work requirements from the order and from what the supervisor or the homeowner says.
tasks.altitude: Finding the written order is shorter when the card is current. The painter still receives the instructions and still determines the requirements.

reach.task: Keep the order card for painting jobs the painter will read
reach.learn: To name the job, the rooms, the colour, and who asked, and to drop a row that is no longer true

evidence.claim: Reading a work order and hearing a supervisor or a homeowner are how the painter learns the job. A card shortens finding the written order. It does not hear the instructions or determine the requirements. Model knowledge.

Remote monitoring such as GPS in a company van needs a legitimate interest, and tracking private use usually fails. This task adds no van tracking. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited guidance.

A log of hours, location, and the job observes presence and performance and needs works-council consent under the cited article. This task adds no such log. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited statute.

assumptions: The boundary is one painting job. Receiving instructions and determining the requirements keep their full time.

Order card fields are job, rooms, colour, and who asked. The producer is the supervisor, when a job is booked or the colour changes. If a row is missing or stale, the painter reads the paper work order inside the lookup. The requirements come from s2 and s3, not from the card.
No location log and no hours log are in this design. The card is paper, so there is no native configuration to test and no custom code.
Card upkeep is the supervisor's 1.0 hours per 100 painter hours on this task. The painter's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether a small firm has a supervisor who writes the card, or the painter copies the order.
How often the homeowner changes the colour after the order is read.
research_questions: Of the painting jobs in a month, how many work orders are current on the card, and how many requirements change after the homeowner speaks?

incremental.description: The painter adds no recurring chore. Reading the order and determining the requirements stay in the steps above.
The supervisor writes the order card by hand when a job is booked or the colour changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the order card has no row, the painter reads the paper work order inside the lookup, so most of that step returns. Receiving instructions and determining the requirements never shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Calculate material amounts and estimate costs from measurements.

steps.what: Read the work orders that list the surfaces to measure.
inputs: order card when the supervisor has written one
outputs: which surfaces the work order names

steps.what: Measure each surface and record the measurements.
inputs: which surfaces the work order names
the coverage printed on the tin
outputs: the measurements for each surface: area or length and height, openings, coats, coverage, and unit price

steps.what: Calculate the amounts of required materials and estimate costs based on those surface measurements.
inputs: the measurements for each surface: area or length and height, openings, coats, coverage, and unit price

steps.what: Check the calculated amounts and the estimated costs against the measurements and record the accepted costs.
inputs: the measurements for each surface: area or length and height, openings, coats, coverage, and unit price
outputs: the accepted material amounts and the accepted estimated costs

tasks.design: The painter measures each surface and writes the area or the length and height, the openings, the coats, the coverage read off the tin, and the unit price. A separate multiply step then calculates the amounts of required materials and estimates the costs from those numbers only. The multiply drafts. It does not run when any of those numbers is missing. The painter checks the draft against the measurements and records the accepted costs. Measuring stays at full time.
tasks.previous_blocker: The painter multiplied area, coats, and coverage by hand, then applied the unit price, and a missed opening or a misread coverage changed the cost.
tasks.enabler_now: Once the painter has written area, openings, coats, coverage, and unit price, the amounts and the cost are arithmetic. A calculation column the firm already keeps can do that arithmetic. Test that column before any custom code.
tasks.still_hard: Measuring the room, reading the coverage off the tin, and deciding whether the draft cost is the one to accept.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing the surface, the openings, and whether the draft matches the room.
tasks.altitude: The painter still measures and still accepts the cost. The multiply only does the arithmetic, and only after the painter has written every number it uses.

reach.task: Write area, openings, coats, coverage, and unit price before the multiply runs
reach.learn: Which of those numbers was blank, so the multiply did not run and the check had to do that sum

evidence.claim: Multiplying measured area, coats, and coverage, then applying a unit price, is arithmetic. The painter still measures and still accepts the cost. Model knowledge.

The cited annex makes high-risk an AI system that allocates tasks from individual behaviour or personal traits, or that evaluates worker performance. A ranking of painters on speed would be that kind of system. This multiply does not do that: it uses the area, coats, coverage, and unit price the painter wrote. Model knowledge of this design; the annex text is the cited source.

assumptions: The boundary is one painting job. Measuring and recording the measurements keep their full time. The multiply is step s3, with its own effort, draft authority, and the painter's gate. The check time sits in s4.

The producer of the multiply inputs is the painter in s2. Fields: area or length and height, openings, coats, coverage read off the tin, and unit price. If coverage or unit price is missing, s3 does not run and does not invent a number. The painter does that sum inside s4.
s3 may use only the numbers s2 wrote for this job. It drafts amounts and costs from those numbers and stops there. It does not rank painters.

The painter's acceptance in s4 binds the figures s3 drafted from that snapshot. If the painter changes a figure in s4, that change voids the machine version and the figures written in s4 are the ones used.
Test a calculation column the firm already keeps before custom code. Order-card upkeep is counted on the work-order task, not again here. This task adds no second card and no focal upkeep.
unknowns: Whether coverage is printed on every tin the firm buys.
How often the unit price is missing until the painter is at the counter.
research_questions: Of the estimates in a month, how many have area, openings, coats, coverage, and unit price written before the multiply runs?

incremental.description: The painter adds no recurring chore. Measuring, the multiply, and the check stay in the steps above.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When coverage or the unit price is missing, the multiply does not run and the painter does that sum inside the check. When the order card has no row, the lookup returns to the paper work order. Measuring never shrinks.

approvals.approved_version: Amounts and costs drafted in s3 from the area or length and height, openings, coats, coverage, and unit price written in s2 for this job. A change written in s4 voids this version.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select and purchase tools or finishes for the surfaces.

steps.what: Read which finishes suit the surfaces to be covered.
inputs: finish card when the stores colleague has written one
outputs: the finishes noted for that surface type, with durability and method

steps.what: Select tools or finishes for those surfaces, considering durability, ease of handling, methods of application, and customers' wishes.
inputs: the finishes noted for that surface type, with durability and method
outputs: the tools or finishes the painter selected

steps.what: Purchase the tools or finishes that were selected.
inputs: the tools or finishes the painter selected

tasks.design: The stores colleague keeps a paper finish card: surface type, finish, durability, and method. The painter reads that card, or the tin and the shelf label when a row is missing, then selects the tools or finishes, considering durability, ease of handling, methods of application, and the customer's wishes, and purchases what was selected. Selecting and purchasing stay at full time. The customer's wishes are not on the card.
tasks.previous_blocker: Which finish suited a surface sat on tins and shelf labels, so each choice started as a search. The customer's wishes are heard only at the job.
tasks.enabler_now: The stores colleague already knows the surface type, the finish, the durability, and the method. Writing those four fields on a card needs no new system and no model.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the finish for this customer, and buying it, stay with the painter.
tasks.human_edge: Judging durability, handling, and the method against what this customer asked for.
tasks.altitude: Finding the finish note is shorter when the card is current. The painter still selects and still purchases.

reach.task: Keep the finish card for surfaces the painter will cover
reach.learn: To name the surface type, the finish, the durability, and the method, and to drop a row that is no longer true

evidence.claim: Selecting a finish and purchasing it are the painter's judgement and the purchase itself. A card shortens finding the finish note. It does not choose the finish or buy it. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The boundary is one set of surfaces to cover. Selecting and purchasing keep their full time.

Finish card fields are surface type, finish, durability, and method. The producer is the stores colleague, when a finish is stocked or dropped. If a row is missing or stale, the painter reads the tin and the shelf label inside the lookup. The customer's wishes are heard in s2, not stored on the card.
The purchase is the painter buying what was selected, in person. The card is paper, so there is no native configuration to test and no custom code.
Card upkeep is the stores colleague's 1.5 hours per 100 painter hours on this task. The painter's own upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether a small firm has a stores colleague, or the painter keeps the card.
How often the chosen finish is one the card does not list.
research_questions: Of the purchases in a month, how many finishes were on the card, and how many changed because of the customer's wishes?

incremental.description: The painter adds no recurring chore. Reading the finish note, selecting, and purchasing stay in the steps above.
The stores colleague writes the finish card by hand when a finish is stocked or dropped.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the finish card has no row, the painter reads the tin and the shelf label inside the lookup, so most of that step returns. Selecting and purchasing never shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The painter still takes the instructions, determines the requirements, measures, checks the figures, selects, and buys. A card only shortens finding the order or the finish note. The multiply only does arithmetic when the painter has written complete numbers, and the painter still accepts the cost.
reach: A supervisor learns to write the job, the rooms, the colour, and who asked on the order card before the painter reads the work order.
The painter's measuring writes the area or the length and height, the openings, the coats, the coverage, and the unit price before the multiply runs.
A stores colleague learns to write the surface type, the finish, the durability, and the method before the painter selects.
skills_to_grow: Open the paper order, the tin, or the shelf label when the card has no row.
Redo a sum that looks odd, and do not accept a draft that does not match the measurements.
Do not let the card or the multiply choose the finish or the price the customer hears.
role.ambitious_version: The painter still takes the instructions, determines the requirements, measures, accepts the cost, selects, and buys. The cards and the multiply do not.
